allow_large: The owner allowed it: five code files plus the agent guide the review rule requires
done_when: At most 2 Forge agent runs (forge work rounds, plan reads and close reviews) run at once on one machine across all repos; the others wait in line first come, first served and print one plain line with their place when they start waiting and each time it changes; a run that dies frees its place; the guide says so. A command-level test starts three runs with stub agents and shows the third waits until one ends, then runs.

findings.body: The queue records the Codex driver's lifetime, rather than the actual app-server's. Existing command-level evidence in tests/test_fix_leftover_app_server_bare_command.py:28–33 kills the driver and Forge and asserts that the app-server remains alive. In that situation, machine.py:69 drops the reservation because both recorded processes are dead, allowing replacement runs while the orphaned Codex agent still consumes memory. This is new evidence beyond the previous Claude-only crash finding. Track the app-server or process-group lifetime so the reservation survives until the agent actually ends.
findings.title: Not done: At most 2 Forge agent runs (forge work rounds, plan reads and close reviews) run at once on one machine across all repos

findings.body: Sending SIGINT to the Forge close process unwinds _attempt, but review.py:531–546 neither terminates nor waits for Autoreview on that path. This finally block nevertheless deletes its reservation unconditionally, and cli.py:123–124 then exits Forge. A waiting run can therefore start while the interrupted review's agent continues running, exceeding the two-agent limit. Preserve reservations whose agents remain alive, or stop and reap the review before releasing its slot.
findings.title: Keep a live review's reservation when Forge is interrupted

findings.body: Autoreview starts at line 531 with its prompt already in argv, but its identity is recorded only afterward. If Forge dies between spawning it and completing started(), the queue still contains agent=None. Another waiting process then removes that entry at machine.py:69 and admits a replacement even though Autoreview is alive. The synchronized queue fixes ticket-publication races, but does not close this launch/registration crash window. Make the child retain its reservation, or gate execution on recorded ownership with cleanup when the parent disappears.
findings.title: Prevent review execution before its ownership is durably recorded

findings.body: The single added test proves mixed work/read/close commands across two repos on normal completion. It has only one waiter, never kills a run, and uses Claude for both work and read. Consequently it cannot detect non-FIFO admission, missing position updates, broken crash release, or removal of the Codex-specific read guard at story.py:228. These are promised runtime behaviors, and the standards require the same behavior tests through both adapters. Extend command-level coverage with multiple waiters and controlled process deaths, asserting admission order, changed positions, and the actual live-agent ceiling.
findings.title: Not done: Command-level proof of FIFO admission, queue-position changes, crash recovery, and both adapters

why: Forge runs on several repos at once can start many workers, readers and reviews together and run a Mac out of memory, stopping live services
